model.rationale: The seat's roughly 27-point Republican lean and Smith's roughly 200-to-1 fundraising edge leave no evidence of a competitive race, and prediction markets price his re-election near 98 percent. With no public polling and no expert ratings to suggest otherwise, the expected margin sits in the low twenties for the incumbent.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary last-minute scandal involving Smith or a surge of outside spending for Reichard would put this district in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jason Smith, the Republican incumbent, runs in a southeastern Missouri district that has leaned roughly 27 points Republican in recent election results. He has raised more than $5.2 million this cycle and holds about $5 million in cash, while Democrat Chris Reichard has raised about $25,000. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot. No public polls or expert race ratings cover this contest, and prediction markets put Smith's chance of re-election near 98 percent.

The financial gap, the district's strong Republican lean, and the absence of any competitive signals point to a comfortable Smith re-election, with the expected margin in the low-to-mid twenties. Reichard has minimal resources to contest the seat, and outside groups have shown no interest here. The forecast treats a Republican win as overwhelmingly likely, with only a small residual chance of an upset.
